objective: Evidence-based assessment of whether HPO trials, outer folds, inner folds, seed count, or cost-ratio grid density can be reduced below the frozen full-budget values without changing scientific conclusions.
base_environment: favorable_hmm_coupled (from environments.py), SPEED-REDUCED for this pilot only
speed_reduction_note: horizon=40, n_agents=3 used instead of the frozen full-scale horizon=250, n_agents=10, PURELY to make the sensitivity comparison tractable within available compute. This substitution is valid for THIS question (convergence/CI-width behavior of the HPO/CV procedure) but NOT a substitute for the full-scale scientific runs themselves. Caveat: reduced scale plausibly has HIGHER per-trial noise (less internal averaging within one trial), making this pilot a conservative (harder) test -- 'keep current value' conclusions are therefore not optimistic.
code_version_note: code/ directory in this experiment's parent project archive contains the exact dtcoa_val package used to produce these results.
seed_generation: All seeds are the literal integers 0..N-1 passed directly as scenario-instance seeds to nested_cv_hpo; no additional randomness in seed selection itself. Internal RNG streams (candidate sampling, fold shuffling) are derived deterministically inside nested_cv_hpo/kfold_split from seed0=0 (the nested_cv_hpo default), which was not overridden in any pilot run.
